label: DAY 14
title: I let a genetic algorithm design my bot. It beat mine by 70%.

scenes.title: Not my bot
scenes.caption: evolved
lines: I didn't write this bot. A genetic algorithm evolved it. And it beats the bot I wrote by seventy percent.

scenes.title: My game: Forager
lines: The game: twenty pellets on a fifteen by fifteen board. A move costs one energy, a pellet gives six, and you only see food three steps away.

scenes.title: The bot I wrote
scenes.caption: mine: nearest pellet
lines: My bot walks to the nearest pellet it can see. When it sees nothing, it wanders at random.
On this board: six pellets, then it starved.

scenes.title: The evolved bot's brain
log: w_visited   cells it has been on
lines: Its brain is four numbers: how much it likes food, old cells, the middle, and walking straight.
Start with sixty random brains. Each generation, the best twelve survive, and the rest are replaced by their kids: mixed numbers, plus a small mutation.

scenes.title: Best brain: pellets per game
lines: Generation zero's best brain ate eight and a half pellets a game.
By generation three, seventeen. After thirty generations, nineteen out of twenty.

scenes.title: 1,000 new boards: pellets per game
lines: Then both played a thousand new boards. Mine: eleven pellets a game. Evolved: eighteen point seven.

scenes.title: Switch one number off
lines: So what did it figure out? I switched its numbers off one at a time.
The biggest drop came from the smallest-looking one: walk straight.

scenes.title: Moves onto a cell it already visited
lines: When it can't see food, it keeps going straight. My random wanderer stepped back onto old cells forty three percent of the time. The evolved one, twenty.

scenes.text: I never told it to walk straight.
scenes.sub: 4 evolution runs, all 4 learned it. What should I evolve next?
lines: I never told it to walk straight. I ran evolution four times, and all four found it.
What should I evolve next? Tell me in the comments.

thumbnail.headline: Evolution beat my code
